# `expect-equal-argument-order`

<!-- rule-docs:header (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
Tier: style · Profile: idiomatic · Default: off · Fixes: fix all · Options: none

Reports `std.testing.expectEqual` called with `(actual, expected)` where a
literal constant is passed as the second argument instead of the first.
<!-- /rule-docs:header -->

## Why it matters

The signature of `std.testing.expectEqual` is `expectEqual(expected: anytype,
actual: anytype) !void`. When test assertions fail, Zig formats error
diagnostics as `expected X, found Y`. Passing arguments in reverse order causes
test failure output to report the expected constant as the found value and vice
versa, creating misleading test reports.

## When it fires

Whenever writing unit test assertions with `std.testing.expectEqual`.

<!-- rule-docs:footer (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
## Example

```zig
const std = @import("std");

test "answer" {
    const value: u32 = 40 + 2;
    try std.testing.expectEqual(value, 42);
}
```
